hook.convey: fold a sheet twice, first fold lying on itself → a paper corner = a quarter turn = a right angle; it becomes a tester for corners around us: a wicket's stump on the ground, the corner of a drawing sheet

use.hi: Cricket mein wicket ke stumps zameen mein seedhe khade hote hain. Stump aur zameen ke beech jo kona banta hai, use aaj hum kaagaz ke ek kone se jaanchenge.
use.en: In cricket, the stumps of a wicket stand straight up in the ground. Today we will test the corner between a stump and the ground with a corner made of paper.

use.hi: Tumhari drawing sheet ke chaaron kone ek jaise hote hain. Kaagaz ko do baar modkar ek kona banao, aur dekho ki woh sheet ke kone par kaise baithta hai.
use.en: All four corners of your drawing sheet are alike. Fold a paper twice to make a corner, and see how it sits on the corner of the sheet.

explain.convey: fold a sheet once, then again so the first fold lies on itself → the corner at the folds = paper corner = a quarter turn = right angle (samkon); four such corners fill one full turn

point.hi: Kaagaz ko ek baar modo, phir dobara aise modo ki pehla mod apne hi upar aa jaaye. Modon par jo kona banta hai, woh paper corner hai. Yeh ek quarter turn hai, aur ise right angle kehte hain.
point.en: Fold a paper once, then fold it again so that the first fold lies on itself. The corner at the folds is a paper corner. It is a quarter turn, and it is called a right angle.

prompt.hi: Board ka paper corner ek quarter turn hai. Aise kitne kone ek ke baad ek rakho toh poora chakkar ban jaata hai?
prompt.en: The paper corner on the board is a quarter turn. How many such corners placed one after another make a full turn?

explain.convey: the test: paper corner's point on the angle's corner → one arm along one edge → look at the OTHER arm: along the second edge = right angle; inside with a gap = smaller, not a right angle; one matching arm alone proves nothing

point.hi: Jaanchne ka tareeka yeh hai. Paper corner ki nok angle ke kone par rakho, aur ek bhuja ko paper ke ek kinaare se milao. Ab doosri bhuja dekho. Woh doosre kinaare par bilkul mile, tabhi right angle hai. Board par paper corner ke saath samosa ki nok bani hai.
point.en: This is how to test. Put the point of the paper corner on the corner of the angle, and line up one arm with one edge of the paper. Now look at the other arm. Only if it matches the second edge exactly is it a right angle. The board shows the paper corner next to the tip of a samosa.

prompt.hi: Samosa ki nok par paper corner rakha. Ek bhuja kinaare par milti hai, doosri paper ke andar reh jaati hai aur gap bachta hai. Kya yeh nok right angle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: The paper corner is put on the samosa tip. One arm matches an edge; the other stays inside the paper with a gap. Is this tip a right angle, yes or no?

explain.convey: a square tile upright → paper corner fits its corner; tile turned to sit tilted → the paper corner still fits the same way → turning moves the corner, never changes its opening; a right angle need not look like an L

point.hi: Baayein ek seedhi tile hai, uske kone mein paper corner fit hota hai. Daayein wahi tile ghuma kar rakhi hai, yeh tirchhi tile hai. Paper corner iske kone mein bhi waise hi fit hota hai, kyunki ghumane se kone ka khulaav nahi badalta.
point.en: On the left is an upright tile; the paper corner fits its corner. On the right the same tile is turned; this is the tilted tile. The paper corner fits its corner the same way, because turning does not change the opening of the corner.

prompt.hi: Ab is tirchhi tile ko thoda aur ghuma do, taaki koi bhi kinaara seedha khada ya leta hua na ho. Kya uske kone ab bhi right angle hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Now turn this tilted tile a little more, so that no edge stands upright or lies flat. Are its corners still right angles, yes or no?

problem.hi: Meera kaagaz ko do baar modkar paper corner banati hai aur teen kone jaanchti hai: ₹10 ke note ka kona, samosa ki nok, aur deewar aur zameen ka kona. Note aur deewar wale kone par paper ke dono kinaare bilkul milte hain. Samosa ki nok paper ke andar reh jaati hai aur gap bachta hai. Inmein se kitne kone right angle hain?
problem.en: Meera folds a paper twice to make a paper corner and tests three corners: the corner of a ₹10 note, the tip of a samosa, and the corner where the wall meets the floor. On the note and the wall corner, both edges of the paper match exactly. The samosa tip stays inside the paper with a gap. How many of these corners are right angles?

givens.hi: paper corner kaagaz ko do baar modkar bana hai
givens.en: the paper corner is made by folding a paper twice

givens.hi: note ke kone par dono kinaare bilkul milte hain
givens.en: on the note's corner both edges match exactly

givens.hi: samosa ki nok andar reh jaati hai, gap ke saath
givens.en: the samosa tip stays inside, with a gap

givens.hi: deewar aur zameen ke kone par dono kinaare bilkul milte hain
givens.en: on the wall–floor corner both edges match exactly

find.hi: kaunse aur kitne kone right angle hain
find.en: which corners are right angles, and how many of them

do.en: First, know what the paper corner is

steps.result: paper corner khud ek right angle hai

why.hi: kaagaz do baar modne se quarter turn ka kona banta hai
why.en: folding a paper twice makes a corner of a quarter turn

steps.result: samosa ki nok right angle se chhoti hai, right angle nahi

why.hi: doosri bhuja paper ke andar reh jaati hai aur gap bachta hai
why.en: the other arm stays inside the paper and a gap is left

prompt.hi: Note ke kone aur deewar wale kone par dono kinaare bilkul milte hain, samosa ki nok par nahi. Toh teeno mein se kitne kone right angle hain?
prompt.en: On the note's corner and the wall corner both edges match exactly; on the samosa tip they do not. So how many of the three corners are right angles?

answer.hi: 2 kone right angle hain, ₹10 ke note ka kona aur deewar aur zameen ka kona, samosa ki nok nahi
answer.en: 2 corners are right angles, the corner of the ₹10 note and the wall–floor corner, not the samosa tip

why.hi: right angle tabhi hai jab paper corner ki dono bhujayein bilkul milein, aur samosa ki nok par doosri bhuja andar reh gayi thi
why.en: it is a right angle only when both arms of the paper corner match exactly, and on the samosa tip the other arm stayed inside

prompt.hi: Ek kone par paper corner rakha. Pehli bhuja kinaare par milti hai, par doosri bhuja paper ke andar hai aur gap bachta hai. Yeh kona right angle se chhota hai, barabar hai ya bada?
prompt.en: A paper corner is put on a corner. The first arm matches an edge, but the second arm is inside the paper with a gap. Is this corner smaller than, equal to or bigger than a right angle?

prompt.hi: Ek square tile zameen par tirchhi rakhi hai. Kya uske kone ab bhi right angle hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A square tile is lying tilted on the floor. Are its corners still right angles, yes or no?

ladder.why: first straight use: which everyday corner (notebook, pizza tip, open fan) matches a paper corner
two metro routes, straight up and straight right → predict the paper corner fits exactly
tilted display boards that the paper corner still fits → right angle judged by fit, not by an upright L

remediation.move: vertex on point → arm 1 on edge 1 → stop and look only at arm 2 against edge 2: on it = right, gap inside = smaller, poking outside = bigger; one matching arm is only half the test

say.hi: Ek bhuja milana sirf aadha kaam hai. Doosri bhuja bhi doosre kinaare par bilkul mile, tabhi woh paper corner jaisa right angle hai.
say.en: Matching one arm is only half the job. Only if the other arm also matches the second edge exactly is it a right angle like the paper corner.

prompt.hi: Paper corner rakha: ek bhuja kinaare par, doosri paper ke bahar nikli. Kya yeh right angle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A paper corner is put on an angle: one arm matches an edge, the other goes outside the paper. Is it a right angle, yes or no?

remediation.move: paper corner held in one corner of a square tile while the tile is turned slowly → ask when the fit stopped → it never stops → the corner is still a right angle in any position

say.hi: Tile ke kone mein paper corner rakho aur tile ko dheere-dheere ghumao. Paper corner kone mein fit hi rehta hai, isliye tirchhi tile ka kona bhi right angle hai.
say.en: Keep a paper corner in the tile's corner and turn the tile slowly. The paper corner stays fitted in the corner, so the corner of the tilted tile is a right angle too.

prompt.hi: Ek kitaab table par tirchhi padi hai. Kya uske kone right angle hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A book is lying tilted on a table. Are its corners right angles, yes or no?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab paper corner se right angle pehchaanna aa gaya. Agle hisse mein dekhenge ki jo angle us par fit nahi hote, unke naam kya hain.
bridgeToNext.en: Now you can spot a right angle with a paper corner. Next we see what the angles that do not fit it are called.

hook.convey: one opening that keeps widening (a car door) → before the paper corner, at it, past it, up to a straight line → three names by comparing with the right angle

use.hi: Car ka darwaza dheere-dheere kholo. Pehle woh thoda sa khulta hai, phir seedha bahar ki taraf, phir aur zyada. Darwaze aur car ke beech ka angle har baar badalta hai.
use.en: Open a car door slowly. First it opens just a little, then straight out, then even more. The angle between the door and the car changes each time.

use.hi: Drawing mein ek ghar banao. Deewar aur zameen ka kona paper corner jaisa hai, par chhat ki nok usse patli hai. Har kone ko paper corner se mila kar uska naam rakhenge.
use.en: Draw a house. The corner of the wall and the ground is like a paper corner, but the tip of the roof is narrower than it. We will compare each corner with the paper corner and name it.

explain.convey: paper corner on angle A → the other arm stays inside with a gap → A smaller than a right angle → acute (nyoon kon); B is a second narrow angle for the child to name

point.hi: Angle A ke kone par paper corner rakho aur ek bhuja milao. A ki doosri bhuja paper ke andar reh jaati hai, gap bachta hai. Toh A right angle se chhota hai. Right angle se chhote angle ko acute angle kehte hain.
point.en: Put the paper corner on the corner of angle A and match one arm. The other arm of A stays inside the paper, with a gap. So A is smaller than a right angle. An angle smaller than a right angle is called an acute angle.

prompt.hi: Ab angle B par paper corner rakho. Ek bhuja kinaare par milti hai, doosri paper ke andar rehti hai. B acute hai ya right angle?
prompt.en: Now put the paper corner on angle B. One arm matches an edge; the other stays inside the paper. Is B acute or a right angle?

explain.convey: paper corner on angle A → the other arm goes outside the paper → A bigger than a right angle, not yet a straight line → obtuse (adhik kon); B is a second wide angle for the child to name

point.hi: Ab is angle A par paper corner rakho aur ek bhuja milao. Doosri bhuja paper ke bahar nikal jaati hai. Toh A right angle se bada hai, par bhujayein abhi seedhi line nahi banatin. Aise angle ko obtuse angle kehte hain.
point.en: Now put the paper corner on this angle A and match one arm. The other arm goes outside the paper. So A is bigger than a right angle, but the arms do not yet make a straight line. Such an angle is called an obtuse angle.

prompt.hi: Angle B ki doosri bhuja bhi paper corner ke bahar nikalti hai, aur dono bhujayein seedhi line nahi banatin. B acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: The other arm of angle B also goes outside the paper corner, and the two arms do not make a straight line. Is B acute or obtuse?

explain.convey: obtuse has an upper limit: arms opening wider and wider until they lie in one straight line = a half turn (aadha chakkar) → obtuse = bigger than a right angle AND smaller than a half turn; the straight line itself is outside obtuse

point.hi: Baayein ek obtuse angle hai. Daayein bhujayein itni khul gayi ki dono ek seedhi line mein aa gayi, yeh aadha chakkar hai. Obtuse angle right angle se bada hota hai, aur aadhe chakkar se chhota.
point.en: On the left is an obtuse angle. On the right the arms have opened so far that they lie in one straight line; this is a half turn. An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle, and smaller than a half turn.

prompt.hi: 6 baje ghadi ki suiyan board ki tarah ek seedhi line banati hain. Kya yeh obtuse angle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: At 6 o'clock the clock hands make a straight line, like the one on the board. Is this an obtuse angle, yes or no?

accept: no, it is a half turn

problem.hi: 5 baje ghadi ki dono suiyon ke beech ka angle acute hai, right angle hai ya obtuse?
problem.en: At 5 o'clock, is the angle between the two clock hands acute, a right angle or obtuse?

find.hi: suiyon ke beech ke angle ka type
find.en: the type of the angle between the hands

do.en: First think of the hands at 3 o'clock

steps.result: 3 baje suiyan right angle banati hain, yaani quarter turn

why.hi: 12 se 3 tak sui poore chakkar ka chauthai hissa ghoomti hai
why.en: from 12 to 3 a hand turns a quarter of a full turn

do.hi: Ab 5 baje ki ghante wali sui dekho
do.en: Now look at the hour hand at 5 o'clock

steps.result: 5 baje ka angle right angle se bada hai, aur aadhe chakkar se chhota

why.hi: 5 number 3 se 2 aage hai, par 6 tak nahi pahuncha, jahan suiyan seedhi line banati hain
why.en: 5 is 2 numbers past 3, but has not reached 6, where the hands make a straight line

prompt.hi: Jo angle right angle se bada aur aadhe chakkar se chhota ho, woh acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: An angle bigger than a right angle and smaller than a half turn: is it acute or obtuse?

answer.hi: 5 baje ghadi ki suiyan obtuse angle banati hain
answer.en: at 5 o'clock the clock hands make an obtuse angle

why.hi: suiyan 3 baje wale right angle se zyada khuli hain, par 6 baje wali seedhi line tak nahi pahunchi
why.en: the hands are open wider than the right angle at 3 o'clock, but have not reached the straight line of 6 o'clock

prompt.hi: Ek khuli kitaab table par poori bichhi hai, dono panne ek seedhi line mein hain. Kya panno ke beech obtuse angle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: An open book lies fully flat on a table; both pages are in one straight line. Is the angle between the pages obtuse, yes or no?

accept: no, it is a half turn

prompt.hi: Angle A right angle se bada hai par seedhi line se chhota. Angle B ki dono bhujayein ek seedhi line mein hain. Inmein obtuse kaunsa hai, A ya B?
prompt.en: Angle A is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line. Both arms of angle B lie in one straight line. Which of these is obtuse, A or B?

prompt.hi: Pizza slice ki nok par paper corner rakha. Ek kinaara mila, doosra andar raha aur gap bacha. Nok acute hai, right angle hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: A paper corner is put on the tip of a pizza slice. One edge matches; the other stays inside with a gap. Is the tip acute, a right angle or obtuse?

ladder.why: scissors opened a little → fits inside the paper corner → acute
a door wider than a right angle but not flat → obtuse, with its upper limit named
predict from 3 o'clock to 4 o'clock → the hour hand moves on, the angle opens past right
scoreboard supports narrower than a paper corner → acute inside a story
two kabaddi flags, one narrower and one wider but less than a straight line → pick the obtuse one

remediation.move: two card arms opened step by step: before the paper corner = acute band, past it = obtuse band, the moment they lie in a straight line = a half turn = the end of the obtuse band; obtuse = between a quarter turn and a half turn, the half turn itself outside

say.hi: Do bhujayein dheere-dheere kholo. Right angle ke baad obtuse shuru hota hai, aur jaise hi bhujayein seedhi line banati hain, woh aadha chakkar hai, obtuse nahi.
say.en: Open two arms slowly. After the right angle, obtuse begins, and as soon as the arms make a straight line it is a half turn, not obtuse.

prompt.hi: Ek folding scale poora khol diya, dono hisse ek seedhi line mein hain. Kya yeh obtuse angle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A folding ruler is opened all the way; both parts are in one straight line. Is this an obtuse angle, yes or no?

accept: no, it is a half turn

remediation.move: vertex on point → arm 1 on edge 1 → look at arm 2 only: inside with a gap = acute, on the edge = right, outside = obtuse → the child names which of the three

say.hi: Ek bhuja milane ke baad doosri bhuja dekho. Andar gap ho toh acute, kinaare par mile toh right angle, aur bahar nikle toh obtuse.
say.en: After matching one arm, look at the other arm. A gap inside means acute, matching the edge means a right angle, and going outside means obtuse.

prompt.hi: Paper corner rakha: ek bhuja kinaare par, doosri andar, gap ke saath. Yeh acute hai, right angle hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: A paper corner is put on an angle: one arm on an edge, the other inside the paper, with a gap. Is this angle acute, a right angle or obtuse?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab teeno naam aa gaye: acute, right aur obtuse. Agle hisse mein dekhenge ki angle ko palatne ya uski bhujayein lambi karne se uska type badalta hai ya nahi.
bridgeToNext.en: Now you know all three names: acute, right and obtuse. Next we see whether flipping an angle or making its arms longer changes its type.

hook.convey: the same V drawn, then the sheet turned upside down; a short twig and a long branch leaving a trunk at the same opening → the angle is the opening between the arms, not where it points or how long its arms are

use.hi: Drawing sheet par ek V draw karo, phir sheet ko ulta ghuma do. Ab V neeche ki taraf hai, par uski dono lakeeron ke beech ka khulaav wahi hai.
use.en: Draw a V on a drawing sheet, then turn the sheet upside down. Now the V points downwards, but the opening between its two lines is the same.

use.hi: Ek chhote plant ki tahni aur ek bade tree ki daali tane se ek jaisa kona bana sakti hain. Daali lambi hai, par uska khulaav tahni jitna hi hai.
use.en: A twig on a small plant and a branch on a big tree can leave their trunks at the same corner. The branch is longer, but its opening is the same as the twig's.

explain.convey: a right angle drawn opening to the right, the paper flipped → it now opens to the left → laid back on the first, it covers it exactly → only the direction changed, the opening and the type stay; the child applies it to a flipped acute angle

point.hi: Kaagaz par ek right angle bana hai jo daayein khulta hai, aur paper corner us par fit hota hai. Ab kaagaz palat do. Angle ab baayein khulta hai. Use pehle wale par rakho toh dono bilkul mil jaate hain, khulaav wahi hai, sirf disha badli.
point.en: A right angle is drawn on paper, opening to the right, and the paper corner fits it. Now flip the paper. The angle now opens to the left. Lay it on the first one and the two match exactly; the opening is the same, only the direction changed.

prompt.hi: Isi tarah ek acute angle daayein khulta hai. Kaagaz palat do toh woh baayein khulta hai. Ab woh acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: In the same way, an acute angle opens to the right. Flip the paper and it opens to the left. Is it acute or obtuse now?

explain.convey: two angles with the same opening, arms 3 cm and 8 cm → the paper corner sits on both the same way → longer arms are only longer lines; the opening, and so the type, does not change

point.hi: Do angle hain. Ek ki bhujayein 3 cm hain, doosre ki 8 cm. Dono par paper corner bilkul fit hota hai. Bhuja ki lambai badhane se lakeer lambi hoti hai, khulaav nahi badalta.
point.en: There are two angles. One has arms of 3 cm, the other 8 cm. The paper corner fits both exactly. Making the arms longer makes the lines longer; it does not change the opening.

prompt.hi: Ek acute angle ki bhujayein 2 cm hain. Khulaav wahi rakhkar bhujayein 9 cm kar di. Ab woh acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: An acute angle has arms of 2 cm. Keeping the same opening, the arms are made 9 cm. Is it acute or obtuse now?

explain.convey: what can change vs what decides: direction and arm length can change; the opening between the arms decides the type → both changes at once still leave the type as it was

point.hi: Baayein woh cheezein hain jo badal sakti hain: disha aur bhuja ki lambai. Daayein woh hai jo angle ka type tay karta hai: sirf khulaav, yaani dono bhujaon ke beech kitna ghumaav hai.
point.en: On the left are the things that can change: the direction and the length of the arms. On the right is what decides the type of the angle: only the opening, that is, how much turn there is between the two arms.

prompt.hi: Ek obtuse angle ko palat diya aur uski bhujayein chhoti kar di, khulaav wahi raha. Ab woh acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: An obtuse angle is flipped and its arms are made shorter; the opening stays the same. Is it acute or obtuse now?

problem.hi: Arjun ek angle banata hai jiski bhujayein 3 cm hain aur jo daayein khulta hai. Paper corner us par bilkul fit hota hai. Kavya wahi khulaav trace karti hai, par bhujayein 8 cm ki banati hai aur drawing palat deti hai, toh uska angle baayein khulta hai. Kavya ka angle kaunsa hai?
problem.en: Arjun draws an angle with arms 3 cm long that opens to the right. A paper corner fits it exactly. Kavya traces the same opening, but makes the arms 8 cm long and flips the drawing, so her angle opens to the left. What type of angle is Kavya's?

givens.hi: Arjun ka angle: bhujayein 3 cm, daayein khulta, paper corner bilkul fit
givens.en: Arjun's angle: arms 3 cm, opens right, the paper corner fits exactly

givens.hi: Kavya ka angle: wahi khulaav, bhujayein 8 cm, baayein khulta
givens.en: Kavya's angle: the same opening, arms 8 cm, opens left

steps.result: Arjun ka angle right angle hai

why.hi: paper corner us par bilkul fit hota hai
why.en: the paper corner fits it exactly

do.hi: Ab dekho Kavya ne kya badla

steps.result: disha aur bhuja ki lambai badli, khulaav wahi raha

why.hi: Kavya ne wahi khulaav trace kiya, sirf drawing palti aur bhujayein lambi ki
why.en: Kavya traced the same opening; she only flipped the drawing and made the arms longer

prompt.hi: Khulaav wahi hai jo Arjun ke right angle ka tha. Toh Kavya ka angle acute hai, right angle hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: The opening is the same as Arjun's right angle. So is Kavya's angle acute, a right angle or obtuse?

answer.hi: Kavya ka angle bhi right angle hai, Arjun ke angle jaisa
answer.en: Kavya's angle is also a right angle, the same type as Arjun's

why.hi: angle ka type sirf bhujaon ke beech ke khulaav se tay hota hai, disha ya bhuja ki lambai se nahi
why.en: the type of an angle is decided only by the opening between its arms, not by its direction or the length of its arms

prompt.hi: Do angle ek hi size ke hain. Ek baayein khulta hai aur ek daayein. Kya dono ek hi type ke hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Two angles are the same size. One opens to the left and one to the right. Are they the same type, yes or no?

prompt.hi: Ek acute angle ki bhujayein 1 cm hain. Khulaav wahi rakhkar bhujayein 15 cm kar di. Ab woh acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: An acute angle has arms of 1 cm. Keeping the same opening, the arms are made 15 cm. Is it acute or obtuse now?

prompt.hi: Ek square photo frame deewar par tirchha latka hai. Uske kone acute hain, right angle hain ya obtuse?
prompt.en: A square photo frame hangs tilted on a wall. Are its corners acute, right angles or obtuse?

ladder.why: same opening, arms 2 cm and 10 cm, someone calls the long one obtuse → compare and correct
error-spot: a tilted square tile said to have no right angles → turning keeps the corners right
explain why a flipped angle is still the same angle → same turn, new direction
V marks pointing up and down with 1 cm and 3 cm arms → both changes at once, type unchanged

remediation.move: a paper angle flipped and laid back on the first one → it covers it exactly → ask whether anything about the opening changed → only the direction did

say.hi: Kaagaz ka angle palat kar pehle wale angle ke upar rakho. Dono bilkul ek doosre par aa jaate hain, toh khulaav wahi hai, bas disha badli.
say.en: Flip the paper angle and lay it on the first angle. The two cover each other exactly, so the opening is the same; only the direction changed.

prompt.hi: Ek obtuse angle daayein khulta hai. Palatne par woh baayein khulta hai. Ab woh acute hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: An obtuse angle opens to the right. Flipped, it opens to the left. Is it acute or obtuse now?

remediation.move: paper corner placed at the vertex of a short-armed and a long-armed copy of the same angle → it sits the same way on both → the arms only run on further; the opening is what the paper corner measures

say.hi: Chhoti bhujaon wale aur lambi bhujaon wale angle, dono ke kone par paper corner rakho. Dono par woh ek jaisa baithta hai, kyunki khulaav same hai.
say.en: Put the paper corner on the corner of the short-armed angle and of the long-armed angle. It sits the same way on both, because the opening is the same.

prompt.hi: Ek right angle ki bhujayein 2 cm se badhakar 20 cm kar di. Ab woh acute hai, right angle hai ya obtuse?
prompt.en: The arms of a right angle are made longer, from 2 cm to 20 cm. Is it acute, a right angle or obtuse now?

remediation.move: a square tile turned slowly while a paper corner stays fitted in one of its corners → ask when the fit stopped → it never stops → the corner stays a right angle, L-shape or not

say.hi: Tile ke kone mein paper corner rakho aur tile ko dheere-dheere ghumao. Paper corner kone mein fit hi rehta hai, toh tirchha kona bhi right angle hai.
say.en: Keep a paper corner in the tile's corner and turn the tile slowly. The paper corner stays fitted in the corner, so a tilted corner is a right angle too.

prompt.hi: Ek square rumaal table par tirchha rakha hai. Uske kone acute hain ya right angle?
prompt.en: A square handkerchief lies tilted on a table. Are its corners acute or right angles?
